title: A 6-Inch Fish Needs Pockets in Its Mouth So Its Teeth Don't Stab Its Brain
subject: fangtooth fish

scenes.text: This fish has teeth so big, its mouth needs pockets so they don't pierce its own brain.
It's the fangtooth. Just six inches long, with the largest teeth in the ocean for its size.
It lives in the dark, mostly between 1,640 and 6,500 feet down, and has been found as deep as 16,000.
When its mouth shuts, the long lower fangs slide into sockets in the roof of its mouth.
Adults hunt fish and squid, rising toward shallower water at night to feed.
Without those pockets, closing its mouth would push fangs into its own head.

description:
The fangtooth fish is only about six inches long, but it has the largest teeth in the ocean relative to its body.
Its teeth are so long that pockets in the roof of its mouth receive them, so they don't pierce its brain.
Would you want to meet this fish in the dark?
first_comment: Imagine teeth this big on a fish smaller than your hand. What deep sea creature should we cover next?
